cards.text: John, the servant who was sent this revelation of Jesus Christ (Revelation 1:1), is on the island of Patmos (Revelation 1:9), and he's just written down the messages to the seven churches (Revelation 2-3). Now he looks and sees a door standing open in heaven. The voice he heard before, the one like a trumpet, calls out, “Come up here,” and promises to show him something.

cards.question: The trumpet-like voice calls John up through the open door in heaven. What does it promise to show him?

answers.text: What must happen after these things
The day and hour of the end
Where the garden of Eden stood

cards.text: At once John is in the Spirit, and he sees a throne standing in heaven with someone seated on it. No waiting room, no take-a-number ticket, no hold music, friend, just straight to the THRONE.
The One seated there looks like jasper and carnelian, and a rainbow that gleams like an emerald circles the throne. Me on my best day, I look like a stamper somebody dropped in the flour bin.
Twenty-four other thrones surround the throne, and on them sit twenty-four elders dressed in white, with golden crowns on their heads. And friend, I thought my tall chef's hat was fancy.

cards.question: Flashes of lightning come from the throne John is seeing. What else comes from it?

cards.text: Friend, my oven timer dings and I hop three feet in the air, gold base and all, so THUNDER would have me hiding under a mixing bowl. Before the throne, seven torches of fire are burning.

cards.question: John says the seven torches of fire burning before the throne are the seven spirits of God.

cards.text: Before the throne is something like a sea of glass, as clear as crystal. Around the throne are four living creatures covered with eyes in front and back, and here I am with two eyes and I STILL can't find my rolling pin.
The first living creature is like a lion, the second like a calf, the third has a face like a man, and the fourth is like an eagle in flight.

Each of the four living creatures has six wings and is covered with eyes all around and within. Day and night they never stop saying the same words about God, no snooze button, no lunch break, NOTHING, and I hit snooze twice before my ovens even warm up.

cards.question: Day and night the living creatures say: “Holy, Holy, Holy, is the Lord God Almighty, who was and is and is to come!” What does that last part tell you about Him?

answers.text: He has always been and always will be
He ruled long ago but has stepped away
He is only now beginning to reign

cards.question: Whenever the living creatures give glory, honor and thanks to the One seated on the throne, the twenty-four elders stay seated on their thrones.
As the twenty-four elders fall down and worship, what do they do with their golden crowns?

answers.text: Hand them to the living creatures

cards.question: The elders tell the Lord God that He is worthy to receive glory and honor and power. What reason do they give?

answers.text: He opened a door in heaven

cards.text: Then John sees a scroll in the right hand of the One seated on the throne. It has writing on both sides and seven seals on it, and friend, I can't open ONE cookie box without a fight.

cards.question: A mighty angel calls out in a loud voice, “Who is worthy to break the seals and open the scroll?” Who in heaven or on earth or under the earth is able to do it?
No one is found worthy to open the scroll or even look inside it. How does John react?

answers.text: He tries to open it himself
He falls on his face in fear

cards.text: Friend, I spent years in the back of a junk drawer waiting for somebody to open it, so I get it. But one of the elders says to John, “Do not weep!” and tells him someone has triumphed to open the scroll and its seven seals.

cards.question: The elder calls the One who has triumphed to open the scroll the Root of David. That's David, Israel's king (2 Samuel 5:3). What else does the elder call Him?

answers.text: The Lion of the tribe of Judah
The Star that comes out of Jacob
The Prophet raised up like Moses

cards.question: After hearing the elder, John looks toward the throne. What does he see standing in the center of it?

answers.text: A lion with a golden crown

cards.text: Let that sit a second, friend: the elder says Lion, John looks, and there stands a Lamb who appeared to have been slain, with seven horns and seven eyes. This Lamb is Jesus, the Lamb of God (John 1:29).

cards.question: The Lamb has seven horns and seven eyes. What does John say they represent?

cards.text: Now the Lamb makes His move and comes to the One seated on the throne.

cards.question: The Lamb waits for the mighty angel to hand Him the scroll.

cards.text: When He takes the scroll, the four living creatures and the twenty-four elders fall down before the Lamb. Each one has a harp, and they're holding golden bowls full of incense.

cards.question: The living creatures and the elders hold golden bowls full of incense before the Lamb. What does John say the incense is?

cards.text: Think about it, friend: I spent years next to receipts nobody needed, and up there the prayers of the saints are held in golden bowls. Then they sing a new song to the Lamb.

cards.question: In their new song, why do they say the Lamb is worthy to take the scroll and open its seals?

answers.text: He was slain and purchased people for God
He is the oldest one in all of heaven
The mighty angel chose Him to open it

cards.question: By His blood the Lamb purchased people for God. Where are those people from?

answers.text: Every tribe and tongue and nation

cards.text: The song goes on: He made them a kingdom and priests to serve our God, and they will reign upon the earth. Me? I got moved from a junk drawer to a cookie planet and I STILL haven't calmed down.

Then John hears the voices of many angels encircling the throne, along with the living creatures and the elders, and their number is myriads of myriads and thousands of thousands. In a loud voice they say: “Worthy is the Lamb who was slain, to receive power and riches and wisdom and strength and honor and glory and blessing!”

cards.question: After the angels' loud praise, John hears even more voices praising Him who sits on the throne and the Lamb. Whose voices are they?

cards.text: Every creature in heaven and on earth and under the earth and in the sea gives praise and honor and glory and power forever and ever to Him who sits on the throne and to the Lamb.
The four living creatures say, “Amen,” and the elders fall down and worship. Hold that thought and keep your apron on, friend, because this story is just getting started.

findings.problem: Stop 1 has 8 story cards and only 7 choice cards.

rule.text: Choice cards are equal to or more than story cards in every stop.

findings.problem: Discovery questions make up most of the choices rather than a few. In stop 1, cards 2, 8, 13, 14 and 15 ask for details that the earlier cards do not help the baker reason out. Stop 2 does the same with cards 2, 3, 5, 6, 12 and 15. A baker who has only seen the earlier cards is largely guessing at the next detail.

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer. The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question. A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

findings.problem: Nine of the stop's ten choice cards are multiple choice, and the only other one is true or false. Multiple choice dominates the stop by a wide margin.

rule.text: No formula. Which question type comes next, the order the types come in and where a blank falls are chosen naturally for each card. They never follow a pattern. No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: The card retells the elder's Lion title from Revelation 5:5 as well as John's sight of the Lamb in Revelation 5:6, but it cites only Revelation 5:6. Its story-card range should begin at Revelation 5:5.

rule.text: Cite exactly what the card uses. Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The question never identifies who is singing. "Their" and "they" depend on earlier cards that are no longer on screen; the question should identify the living creatures and elders as the singers.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.
